title: Predicting genome-wide functional constraints with GPN-Star.
data_url: https://huggingface.co/songlab (datasets: clinvar_vs_benign, ukb_finemapped_coding, ukb_finemapped_nc_traitgym, omim_traitgym, flybase_lethal, celegans_lethal, mmrdb, caendr, gnomad_balanced, gpn-star-scores)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed every songlab Hugging Face dataset and the 19 GPN-Star model checkpoints (MIT licence). Downloaded and opened 8 benchmark test.parquet files: clinvar_vs_benign 50,164 rows (22,254 Pathogenic / 27,910 Benign), ukb_finemapped_coding 2,221 (224 positive), ukb_finemapped_nc_traitgym 11,400 (1,140), omim_traitgym 3,380 (338), flybase_lethal 42,078 (2,929; 91 duplicate variants), celegans_lethal 22,255 (72), mmrdb mouse 504,392 (433; 65 duplicates), caendr worm 650,238 (442,453 True). Each has chrom/pos/ref/alt/consequence/label; no nulls except OMIM id. Prediction files are one 'score' column aligned to the test rows by position. I recomputed AUROC (area under the ROC curve) myself: ClinVar AlphaMissense 0.955, GPN-Star-V100 0.925, CADD 0.909, PhyloP 0.851; fly lethal GPN-Star 0.984, PhyloP 0.934 (sign flipped); worm lethal GPN-Star 0.991 (AUPRC 0.73), PhyloP 0.95; mouse MMRdb GPN-Star 0.855 (AUPRC 0.29), PhyloP 0.77. Alignment files: worm 135-way 1.45 GB, fly 124-way 2.08 GB (metadata only). Genome-wide score set is tens of GB of parquet/BigWig (metadata only).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was available (paywalled, no PMCID, no Europe PMC full text). How the labels were assembled (what counts as a negative in the lethal and MMRdb sets, what the CaeNDR boolean label means) is not documented in the 230-byte dataset READMEs and was not read in the paper. The paper's own reported benchmark numbers were not retrieved, so my AUROCs are not checked against them.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: all benchmark parquets download from Hugging Face without login; MIT licence on datasets and models.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked: every test.parquet has a 'label' column (boolean, or Pathogenic/Benign for ClinVar); nothing needs constructing.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: inputs are genomic coordinates plus ref/alt alleles, not sequences; one reference-genome download resolves them, and precomputed model scores are already provided as ready features.

a4_units_stated.note: Labels are binary, so units barely matter; score files lack a stated sign convention (higher means constrained for PhyloP, lower for GPN-Star log-likelihood ratio), which I had to infer.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked: ClinVar set 50,164 rows; fly lethal 42,078 with 2,929 positives; mouse 504,392 with only 433 positives; worm lethal only 72 positives.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~100 MB of benchmark and score parquets
a6_fits_laptop.note: A head on precomputed scores fits easily; computing new GPN-Star embeddings needs multi-GB whole-genome alignments and likely a GPU, so that route is out.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Only the abstract was readable, which gives no counts; Hugging Face file row counts are internally consistent (prediction files match test rows exactly).

a8_label_provenance.note: ClinVar labels come from clinical curation; lethal labels from genetic screens; fine-mapped labels from statistical fine-mapping (a model, but not a sequence model). CaeNDR and gnomAD labels appear derived from allele frequency, which is a proxy, so avoid those sets.

B1.why: Checked: one test table per benchmark plus one score file per model, joined by row order, not a key.

B2.why: Checked: all parquets parsed first try with pandas/pyarrow.

B3.why: Each benchmark has its own label source (ClinVar curation, screens, fine-mapping); comparable only within a benchmark.

B4.why: Checked: binary labels, no censored values.

B5.why: Checked: 91 duplicate variants in fly set, 65 in mouse; zero in human sets.

B6.why: Checked: READMEs are about 230 bytes with no column descriptions or label definitions.

C1.why: Cross-species transfer is informative either way, but fly/worm AUROC is already 0.98-0.99, leaving little to learn.

C2.why: GPN-Star, AlphaMissense, CADD, PhyloP all open and evaluated on these exact benchmarks by the authors.

C3.why: Only weak angle: mouse MMRdb set where GPN-Star AUPRC is 0.29 (my computation).

C4.why: Lethality screens and clinical curation are costly, but genome-wide scores already exist free.

C5.why: Checked: per-model prediction files give ready baselines; I computed AUROCs from them.

D1.why: Checked: 19 GPN-Star checkpoints on Hugging Face, MIT licence.

D2.why: Embeddings need multi-GB alignments (worm 1.45 GB, human far larger) and likely GPU; precomputed scores only.

D3.why: Checked: MIT on models and benchmarks, Apache-2.0 on genome-wide scores.

E1.why: Hold-out chromosome or held-out species splits are possible from the chrom column.

E2.why: Checked: 5-20 chromosomes per species and six species.

E3.why: Consequence-class base rate (nonsense vs missense) is an obvious dummy.

E4.why: No replicate labels; noise floor not estimable.

E5.why: Nonsense variants should outrank missense for lethality; PhyloP alone gives AUROC 0.93-0.95 (my computation).

E6.why: Label shuffling and score-block ablation are trivial on these tables.

E7.why: Checked: lethal/mutant sets exist for fly, worm and mouse, enabling train-one-species, test-another.

E8.why: I computed AUROCs but could not read the paper's numbers to confirm they match.

G1.why: Checked: chrom/pos/ref/alt coordinates; human coding set also has Ensembl gene IDs.

G2.why: AlphaGenome or gnomAD constraint joinable on coordinates (genome build hg38 implied by GPN-Star naming).

G3.why: One variant per row; coordinate joins are one-to-one.

G4.why: Adding regulatory predictions to conservation is already done in TraitGym; marginal question.

H1.why: Checked: every set has both labels, though negatives are often population variants, not tested-and-tolerated.

H2.why: Checked: human, mouse, fly, worm (plus chicken, Arabidopsis sets listed).

H3.why: Claim is precise: ranks screen-recovered lethal alleles above population variants in model organisms.

H4.why: Label construction undocumented in READMEs; paper text not readable.

I1.why: Model-organism geneticists and the Song lab; no group with an open decision identified.

I2.why: Genome-wide GPN-Star scores already serve users; a stacked head changes little.

I3.why: AUPRC (area under precision-recall curve) roughly matches variant prioritisation.

I4.why: Single conservation score already reaches AUROC 0.93-0.95 on fly/worm sets (my computation).

J1.why: Mostly stacking precomputed scores; little representation learning on a laptop.

J2.why: Variant-effect intuition is moderately available; label definitions are opaque.

J3.why: Cross-species benchmark table of existing scores is shareable at any stage.

existing_models.name: GPN-Star (this paper; phylogeny-aware DNA language model)
existing_models.score_and_split: My recomputation from released predictions: ClinVar missense AUROC 0.925; fly lethal 0.984; worm lethal 0.991; mouse MMRdb 0.855 (AUPRC 0.29). Zero-shot, no training split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved; abstract notes task-dependent trade-offs between recent and deep evolutionary timescales.

existing_models.name: AlphaMissense (protein missense predictor)
existing_models.score_and_split: ClinVar missense AUROC 0.955 on 47,783 scored rows (my computation from released predictions).

existing_models.name: PhyloP (classical conservation score)
existing_models.score_and_split: ClinVar AUROC 0.851; fly lethal 0.934; worm lethal 0.95; mouse 0.77 (my computation).

existing_models.name: TraitGym benchmark (Song lab; compares CADD, GPN-MSA, Enformer, Borzoi, Evo2)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search summary only: alignment models best on Mendelian traits, Borzoi/Enformer on complex non-disease traits; numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Search summary: Evo2 struggles on enhancer variants.

existing_models.name: ProteoCast (fly missense predictor)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet: classifies 85% of known fly lethal mutations as impactful vs 13-18% of population variants; split not read.

backbone.name: GPN-Star (25M-200M parameter alignment-based DNA language model)
backbone.hardware: Embedding needs multi-GB whole-genome alignments and probably a GPU; laptop route is a head on precomputed scores only

integration.partner_dataset: AlphaGenome precomputed variant effects or gnomAD constraint
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does adding regulatory-activity predictions to evolutionary constraint help rank causal non-coding variants, a question TraitGym already largely addresses.

controls.positive_control: Nonsense variants should rank above missense for lethality; PhyloP alone reproduces AUROC about 0.93-0.95 on fly/worm sets.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels within consequence class; performance should fall to the consequence-class base rate.
controls.external_validation: Train on fly lethal, test on worm lethal and mouse MMRdb (held-out species).

honest_claim_h3: A head stacked on GPN-Star and conservation scores ranks screen-recovered lethal alleles above natural population variants in model organisms, among variants the screens happened to recover.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use precomputed evolutionary-conservation scores and variant type to predict which DNA changes are lethal, training on fly and testing on worm and mouse.
plain_idea.train_on: Per variant: several precomputed conservation and language-model scores plus the variant's effect class; 42,078 fly variants (2,929 lethal), verified.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the variant is a known lethal or disease-causing allele, a label taken from genetic screens (fly, worm, mouse) or clinical curation (ClinVar), as released by the authors.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would tell model-organism geneticists whether constraint scores transfer across species; but the authors' own model already scores 0.98-0.99 AUROC on fly and worm.

ml_idea: Cross-species stacking: logistic-regression or gradient-boosted head on released GPN-Star, PhyloP and PhastCons scores plus consequence, trained on one species' lethal set and tested on the others; only mouse MMRdb (AUPRC 0.29) has headroom.

effort.compute_note: Estimated: benchmark tables are under 60 MB each and I loaded and scored them in seconds; new GPN-Star embeddings were not attempted because they need multi-GB alignments.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Compute stacked-head AUPRC on mouse MMRdb with chromosome hold-out; if it does not clearly beat GPN-Star's 0.29, nothing is left to claim.

verdict_reason: Already well covered: the authors' open, MIT-licensed model is evaluated on every released benchmark, reaching AUROC 0.98-0.99 on fly and worm lethal sets in my recomputation, and the human sets are crowded with open baselines (AlphaMissense, CADD). Only the mouse set has headroom, with 433 positives and undocumented label construction.
